.NEAR TERM /UNTIL 6 AM THURSDAY MORNING/...
Main Highlights through Tonight: 

- Flood Watch is in effect for Flagler, Putnam, St. Johns, Clay,
  and Duval counties through Early Friday Evening. 

- Persistent, Gusty Onshore Winds will Result in Increasing
  Coastal and Marine Impacts into the Upcoming Weekend.

Afternoon surface analysis depicts strong high pressure (1035
millibars) that was positioned along the spine of the 
Appalachians, with this feature wedging down the southeastern 
seaboard. Meanwhile, coastal troughing remains situated over the
near shore Atlantic waters adjacent to our local coastline. 
Otherwise, a wavy stationary frontal boundary was stalled over 
the southeast Gulf, extending eastward across the FL Keys and 
northwestern Bahamas. Aloft..."Rex" blocking extends from the 
eastern Great Lakes southward to the eastern Gulf, featuring 
ridging over the Ohio Valley and a cutoff trough over the 
western FL panhandle and the southeastern Gulf. Latest GOES-East
derived Total Precipitable Water imagery indicates that PWATs 
were around 1.25 inches across interior southeast GA, ranging to
around 1.5 inches across northeast and north central FL. 
Deepening east- southeasterly low and mid level flow around the 
aforementioned cutoff trough was combining with the presence of 
the coastal trough to create strong isentropic lift across our 
area, and bands of moderate to occasionally heavy rain band 
frequently traversing the I-95 corridor, with activity moving 
north- northwestward. Light to occasionally moderate rainfall 
was also progressing inland. Thick low and mid level cloud cover
continues to overspread our region this afternoon, keeping 
temperatures in the 60s to lower 70s, while dewpoints ranged 
from the lower 50s for inland locations near the Altamaha River 
in southeast GA to the mid and upper 60s across north central 
and coastal northeast FL. 

Our local pressure gradient will continue to tighten this
afternoon and evening as pressures gradually lower over south 
FL and the Keys along the stationary frontal boundary and strong
high pressure continues to wedge down the southeastern 
seaboard. Wind speeds may increase to near Wind Advisory levels 
late this afternoon and evening at the northeast FL beaches, 
where speeds will become sustained at 20-25 mph with occasional 
gusts of 35-40 mph possible. Meanwhile, deepening east-
southeasterly low and mid level flow will provide for warm air 
advection and gradually increasing moisture levels, with strong 
isentropic lift aiding in the development of moderate to 
occasionally heavy bands of rainfall that will primarily impact 
the I-95 and U.S. Highway 17 corridors through tonight. A Flood 
Watch remains posted for portions of northeast and north central
FL, generally for locations east of U.S. Highway 301, where an 
additional 1-2 inches of rainfall with locally higher amounts 
are expected to fall through tonight. The threat for flooding at
coastal locations will be maximized during times of high tide 
that occur early this afternoon and then overnight, when 
rainfall runoff will be hindered by higher water levels. 
Gradually cooling temperatures aloft associated with the cutoff 
trough over the FL panhandle may support a few embedded 
thunderstorms this evening and tonight, mainly over the Atlantic
coastal waters south of St. Augustine. Highs today will 
generally remain in the 65-70 degree range across our region, 
while warm air advection overnight keeps lows in the 60s, except
upper 50s for inland locations from Waycross north and 
westward.

&&

.SHORT TERM /6 AM THURSDAY MORNING THROUGH FRIDAY NIGHT/...
Main Highlights This Period: 

- Coastal hazards including high risk for rip currents, high 
surf, and very breezy onshore winds. 

- Heavy rainfall and localized flooding potential continues along 
the northeast Florida coast and St Johns River basin with a Flood 
Watch in effect.

Surface high pressure will remain centered to the north this
period. Troughing will be located over the coastal waters 
Thursday. The trough is expected to develop into a deepening low
Friday into Friday night to the southeast. Showers will prevail
over much of the area this period, especially near the coast. 
Convergence will lead to banding of these showers, which could 
result in locally heavier rainfall. The greatest chance for 
flooding rain will be over coastal areas of NE FL. 

High temperatures will be near average, with lows above average 
this period.

&&

.LONG TERM /SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Main Highlights This Period: 

- Above average rainfall chances return by middle of next week. 

High pressure will remain to the north northeast Saturday into 
Saturday night, as northward moving low passes to the east.
Coastal showers will linger Saturday into Saturday night, as 
moisture wraps around the low. 

The low will move away to the northeast Sunday, helping to push 
drier air southeast into forecast area. Sunday is expected to be
a dry day. 

The dry weather is expected to persist Monday into Tuesday as a
weak  front moves through. 

Strong high pressure will build to the north Wednesday, with a 
trough over the coastal waters. This will result in another 
period with moist onshore flow.

Temperatures will be well above seasonal levels Friday night,  
otherwise will trend near or a little above average this period.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z THURSDAY THROUGH 00Z FRIDAY/...
Brief period of VFR conds at CRG/JAX/VQQ/GNV where there is a 
temporary break in the rainfall, while IFR conds continue at SSI for 
a few more hours, while SGJ will remain locked down in IFR conds 
with gusty winds to 30-35 knots through the TAF period. SSI will 
briefly improve tonight by 04-06Z, while the current TAF sites at 
VFR conds will slowly deteriorate in the 06-09Z time frame as the 
next rain band shifts northward and remains in place with generally 
IFR conds and gusty winds through most of the rest of the TAF period 
on Wednesday. This will happen at SSI as well by the 12-15Z time 
frame on Wednesday. More uncertain in any timing of lower conds 
towards the end of the TAF period from 18-24Z, but for now have 
trended towards the lower conds. Gusty NE winds at 10-15 knots 
inland will increase back closer to 15G20-25 knots with the next 
rain band on Wednesday, while gusty NE winds 15-20G25-30 knots will 
continue through the period at coastal terminals.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisory conditions will continue through at least 
Saturday night across our local waters, with periods of Gale 
Force wind gusts possible throughout this extended duration 
northeasterly wind flow event. Strong high pressure situated 
over the Mid-Atlantic states will continue to wedge down the 
southeastern seaboard through Saturday before weakening late 
this weekend. Coastal troughing positioned over our near shore 
waters will continue to develop widespread rainfall, with a few 
embedded thunderstorms possible through Friday. Otherwise, low 
pressure developing near the northern Bahamas on Friday will 
accelerate north-northeastward along the Gulf Stream waters 
adjacent to the southeastern states this weekend, with this 
system potentially acquiring subtropical characteristics as it 
strengthens and moves further away from our local waters. 
Prevailing winds will shift to northerly by Saturday afternoon 
and then northwesterly on Sunday, allowing seas to gradually 
subside by late in the weekend.

Rip Currents / High Surf: Breakers building to 6-10 feet at the  
northeast FL beaches will maintain a high surf advisory through 
at least Sunday morning, and a high rip current risk will 
continue through the upcoming weekend at all area beaches.

Rip Currents / High Surf: Breakers building to 6-10 feet at the 
northeast FL beaches will maintain a high surf advisory through at 
least Sunday morning, and a high rip current risk will continue 
through the upcoming weekend at all area beaches.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
The region will be between high pressure to the north and
troughing  to the south through Friday. Low pressure is 
expected to develop Friday night to the southeast. This low will
track northward and pass east of the area Saturday. As the low 
tracks away to the northeast Sunday, drier air will move 
southeast into area. A weak front will move southeast across 
area early next week. Strong high pressure will build to the 
north middle of next week, with troughing over the coastal 
waters. 

FOG POTENTIAL AND OTHER WEATHER REMARKS: Significant fog is not 
expected Tonight. Flood Watch is in effect for St. Johns, Flagler, 
Duval, Clay, and Putnam counties through Friday night.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
A significant rainfall event will continue along the I-95 and 
U.S. Highway 17 corridor through at least Friday night as 
multiple rounds of heavy rainfall impacts portions of northeast 
and north central FL, extending into portions of coastal 
southeast GA. Additional rainfall amounts of 3-6 inches, with 
locally higher amount of 6-10 inches will be possible within the
Flood Watch area. Currently, the forecast rainfall amounts are 
broadly 4" to 8" for The Weather Prediction Center has 
maintained a "Slight" Risk (level 2 of 4) of Excessive Rainfall 
through Thursday for locations east of U.S. Highway 301, with a 
"Moderate" (Level 3 of 4) for locations along and east of the 
St. Johns River on Friday, when saturated soils will likely lead
to that heightened risk as rainfall runoff increases.

With the potential for several inches of additional rainfall
through Saturday, the National Water Prediction Center has 
highlighted the St Johns River and I-95 Corridor through Duval 
County with a "Limited" potential for river/small stream 
flooding with localized areas where considerable river flood 
impacts may develop. Please remain aware of the forecast as 
rainfall totals may change as we proceed through this multi-day 
rainfall/flood event.
